title: Ops pocket journal - Elliot (oncall) 2026-03-22
content:
Context / quick summary:
- Night window (02:10–03:30 UTC) saw a short-lived spike in DB connection errors affecting the retriever and embeddings backfills. Pages fired: DB-conn-spike-usw2 (pager sequence 1 -> escalated).
- Initial mitigation: scaled connection pool in service-prod-retriever by +50% at 02:18 UTC, routed some traffic to replica-read-only. Error rate dropped by 75% around 02:25 UTC.
- Root cause hypothesis: transient network flaps between app nodes and primary DB in us-west2 (cloud provider incident related to router flaps). Need follow-ups to confirm and harden.

Timeline (notes to self):
- 02:12 UTC: first alert (5xx db connection errors > 20% for 1m). Pager -> me.
- 02:15 UTC: looked at /alerts/db-conn-spike dashboard -> spike concentrated on retriever service, pod restarts low.
- 02:17 UTC: checked provider status; saw network maintenance message in us-west2 region (ticket referenced by provider: NET-9938).
- 02:18 UTC: scaled service-prod-retriever pool to 6 -> 9 (k8s rollout).
- 02:20 UTC: re-routed non-critical embedding backfills to standby region (manual policy).
- 02:25 UTC: error rate stabilized.
- 02:45 UTC: postmortem notes started and SRE-4897 created.

Commands and short outputs I ran (copying for runbook):
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=retriever -o wide
  -> pods healthy, no mass restarts, ready counts fine
- kubectl -n prod logs deploy/retriever --since=10m | grep -i "connection refused" | head -n 5
  -> repeated "could not connect to primary-db: connection refused" lines, then gaps
- psql "host=primary-db-usw2 user=redwood_app" -c "select now(), count(*) from pg_stat_activity;"
  -> connection succeeded locally from bastion (45 active connections)
- sudo journalctl -u node-network-daemon -n 200 | grep -i err
  -> jitter on iface eth1 timestamps: 02:11–02:18 UTC

Preliminary root cause (working hypothesis):
- Provider-level router flaps caused packet loss between some app AZs and the primary DB instance. Some app pods retried aggressively and exhausted ephemeral connection slots; combined with a conservative healthcheck and low pool size this surfaced as a sharp error rate.
- Evidence: provider status note + host-level network jitter + logs showing intermittent connection refused rather than DB internal errors.

Immediate follow-ups (actionable, owners, due):
- [ ] Update retriever service runbook to include auto-scaling of connection pools under error-rate anomalies (owner: Elliot, due: 2026-03-26).
- [ ] Add a synthetic canary that periodically opens 50 concurrent DB connections from each AZ to measure failover latency (owner: Samir, due: 2026-04-02).
- [ ] Adjust alert thresholds to include absolute connection refused counts vs. percent error (owner: Maya, due: 2026-03-29). Ticket: SRE-4897.
- [ ] Validate whether primary DB has connection slot limits -> coordinate with DB eng to add metric export for connection queue length (owner: DB-Infra, linked in ticket).
- [ ] Update runbook: include provider incident mapping and steps to route backfills to standby region (owner: Elliot, due: 2026-03-24).

Runbook TODOs (notes to implement):
- Add quick commands section: one-liners to scale connection pool (kubectl patch deployment ...), reroute backfill traffic (feature-flag toggle web UI path).
- Add playbook entry: "If provider reports network maintenance in region, immediately run canary -> if errors confirmed, reduce write-heavy traffic + send backfill to standby".
- Add post-incident checklist template: record provider incident ID, snapshot prometheus graphs, capture sample logs, create follow-up ticket for DB team if connections near limit.

Outstanding questions / research items:
- Did any of the retriever pods hit ulimit or ephemeral port exhaustion? Need to check node sockstat and netstat dumps for 02:10–02:30 window (todo).
- Are client-side retry backoffs aggressive? Could we smooth out retry logic to avoid thundering herd in transient net issues? Follow-up with lib team owning DB client.
- Should we consider moving primary DB to multi-az failover with faster detection? Cost/benefit ask for infra roadmap.

Notes to self (less formal):
- Remember to sync with product team about backfill behavior; they want high throughput but also stability. Keep a small doc explaining tradeoffs.
- Quick win: add metric that counts "connection refused" distinct from query errors to make alerts actionable.

Post-incident quick log for handoff:
- Left to next oncall: check SRE-4897 progress, confirm synthetic canary PR, and validate alerts after threshold change. Slack: ping @maya if anything pops at night.

Random scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Could we have a lightweight regional proxy pool that holds persistent DB connections and multiplexes queries? Might reduce churn when provider jitter occurs. Prototype idea worth exploring with infra.

Signed: Elliot (oncall)

---
Revision notes: 2026-03-23: added ticket refs, scheduled follow-ups, removed a bunch of noisy logs for brevity.
